text.p: Mexican packaging firm Empaques Ponderosa SA said on Monday its nine-month net profit rose to 180 million pesos versus 87 million pesos during the same period a year ago.
The company said in a statement that its operating profit rose to 210.6 million pesos during the first nine months, up 10 percent versus the same period the previous year.
It also said in the statement that it was negotiating a syndicated loan worth $70 million to refinance its debt and boost output.

The company said its net sales hit 646.7 million pesos during the first nine months, off about 7 percent compared to the same period last year. The company said lower sales were due to a stronger peso, which cut into exports.
Export sales fell 8 percent, while domestic sales grew seven percent, the company said.
Gross profit was 259 million pesos, up 12 percent versus the first nine months of 1995. It said the gross margin improved because of lower cost fibers used in the packaging business.
The company said the new syndicated loan would help it refinance some $50 million in Eurobonds that come due in December.
